{{Nihongo|'''Toshiki Tajima'''|田島俊樹|Tajima Toshiki|born January 18, 1948|lead=yes}}<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=田島俊樹 略歴|url=https://www.jaea.go.jp/02/press2006/p06120601/hosoku1.html|access-date=2020-06-06|website=www.jaea.go.jp|language=ja}}</ref> is a Japanese [[Theoretical physics|theoretical plasma physicist]] known for pioneering the [[Laser-wakefield acceleration|laser wakefield acceleration]] technique with [[John M. Dawson]] in 1979.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Tajima|first1=T.|last2=Dawson|first2=J. M.|date=1979|title=Laser Electron Accelerator|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=43|issue=4|pages=267–270|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.43.267|bibcode=1979PhRvL..43..267T|issn=0031-9007}}</ref> The technique is used to [[Particle acceleration|accelerate particles]] in a plasma and was experimentally realized in 1994,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nakajima|first1=K|last2=Kawakubo|first2=T|last3=Nakanishi|first3=H|last4=Ogata|first4=A|last5=Kato|first5=Y|last6=Kitagawa|first6=Y|last7=Kodama|first7=R|last8=Mima|first8=K|last9=Shiraga|first9=H|last10=Suzuki|first10=K|last11=Zhang|first11=T|date=1994|title=A proof-of-principle experiment of laser wakefield acceleration|journal=Physica Scripta|language=en|volume=T52|issue=T52|pages=61–64|doi=10.1088/0031-8949/1994/t52/009|bibcode=1994PhST...52...61N|s2cid=250779537|issn=0031-8949}}</ref> for which Tajima received several awards such as the [[Nishina Memorial Prize]] (2006), the [[Enrico Fermi Prize]] (2015), the Robert R. Wilson Prize (2019), the [[Hannes Alfvén Prize]] (2019) and the [[Charles Hard Townes Award]] (2020).

Tajima is currently a professor of the [[University of California, Irvine]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Toshiki Tajima {{!}} UCI Physics and Astronomy|url=https://www.physics.uci.edu/people/toshiki-tajima|access-date=2020-06-06|website=www.physics.uci.edu}}</ref> and is the Chief Science Officer of [[TAE Technologies]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=TAE Technologies {{!}} Management Team|url=https://tae.com/company/management-team/|access-date=2020-06-06|website=tae.com}}</ref> His works involve [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]],<ref>{{Citation|last=Tajima|first=Toshiki|chapter=Geometry|date=2018|title=Computational Plasma Physics|pages=268–297|publisher=CRC Press|doi=10.1201/9780429501470-10|isbn=978-0-429-50147-0}}</ref> [[laser physics]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nakajima|first1=K.|last2=Fisher|first2=D.|last3=Kawakubo|first3=T.|last4=Nakanishi|first4=H.|last5=Ogata|first5=A.|last6=Kato|first6=Y.|last7=Kitagawa|first7=Y.|last8=Kodama|first8=R.|last9=Mima|first9=K.|last10=Shiraga|first10=H.|last11=Suzuki|first11=K.|date=1995|title=Observation of Ultrahigh Gradient Electron Acceleration by a Self-Modulated Intense Short Laser Pulse|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=74|issue=22|pages=4428–4431|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.74.4428|pmid=10058504|bibcode=1995PhRvL..74.4428N|issn=0031-9007|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/277813}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Pisin|last2=Tajima|first2=Toshi|date=1999|title=Testing Unruh Radiation with Ultraintense Lasers|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=83|issue=2|pages=256–259|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.83.256|bibcode=1999PhRvL..83..256C|issn=0031-9007}}</ref> [[nuclear fusion]], [[plasma astrophysics]],<ref>{{Cite book|last=Tajima, Toshiki.|title=Plasma astrophysics|date=1997|publisher=Addison-Wesley|oclc=988844392}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Tajima|first1=T.|last2=Sakai|first2=J.|last3=Nakajima|first3=H.|last4=Kosugi|first4=T.|last5=Brunel|first5=F.|last6=Kundu|first6=M. R.|date=1987|title=Current loop coalescence model of solar flares|journal=The Astrophysical Journal|volume=321|page=1031|doi=10.1086/165694|bibcode=1987ApJ...321.1031T|issn=0004-637X}}</ref> [[accelerator physics]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Henig|first1=A.|last2=Steinke|first2=S.|last3=Schnürer|first3=M.|last4=Sokollik|first4=T.|last5=Hörlein|first5=R.|last6=Kiefer|first6=D.|last7=Jung|first7=D.|last8=Schreiber|first8=J.|last9=Hegelich|first9=B. M.|last10=Yan|first10=X. Q.|last11=Meyer-ter-Vehn|first11=J.|s2cid=11560750|date=2009|title=Radiation-Pressure Acceleration of Ion Beams Driven by Circularly Polarized Laser Pulses|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=103|issue=24|article-number=245003|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.103.245003|pmid=20366205|arxiv=0908.4057|bibcode=2009PhRvL.103x5003H|issn=0031-9007}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mourou|first1=Gerard|last2=Brocklesby|first2=Bill|last3=Tajima|first3=Toshiki|last4=Limpert|first4=Jens|date=2013|title=The future is fibre accelerators|journal=Nature Photonics|volume=7|issue=4|pages=258–261|doi=10.1038/nphoton.2013.75|bibcode=2013NaPho...7..258M|s2cid=15947736 |issn=1749-4885}}</ref> and [[Medical physics|medical applications of physics]].

== Early life and career ==
Tajima was born in the [[Aichi Prefecture|Aichi prefecture]] of Japan in 1948.<ref name=":0" /> He graduated from the [[University of Tokyo]] with a [[bachelor's degree]] in 1971 and a [[master's degree]] in 1973. He then received his doctorate from the [[University of California, Irvine]] in 1975, and became a post-doctoral student at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]]. In 1980, he became a professor at the [[University of Texas at Austin]], where he remained until 2001. 

From 1998 to 2001, Tajima was Special Assistant to the Associate Director at the [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]], and from 2000 to 2002 he worked at the [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory]]. From 2002, he was director of the Kansai Photon Science Institute of the [[Japan Atomic Energy Agency]], and from 2008 to 2011 he was a professor at [[LMU Munich]]. He has also been at the [[KEK|KEK accelerator]] since 2008. He is currently a Rostoker Chair Professor at the [[University of California, Irvine]].

Tajima was Chairman of the International Committee for Ultrahigh Intensity Lasers (ICUIL) and Deputy Director of the International Center for Zetta-Exawatt Science and Technology (IZEST) at [[École Polytechnique]] (with director [[Gérard Mourou]]).<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Tajima|first1=T.|last2=Mourou|first2=G.|s2cid=15488011|date=2002|title=Zettawatt-exawatt lasers and their applications in ultrastrong-field physics|journal=Physical Review Special Topics - Accelerators and Beams|volume=5|issue=3|article-number=031301|doi=10.1103/physrevstab.5.031301|arxiv=physics/0111091|bibcode=2002PhRvS...5c1301T|issn=1098-4402}}</ref> He was Blaise Pascal Professor and Einstein Professor at the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].

Tajima is also the Chief Science Officer of [[TAE Technologies]], a company founded in 1998 that deals with [[Aneutronic fusion|aneutronic fusion power]].<ref name=":1" />

== Honors and awards ==
Tajima is a fellow of the [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]]{{Citation needed|date=June 2020}} and of The Optical Society.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Toshiki Tajima {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/History/Biographies/bios/Toshiki_Tajima |access-date=2024-09-25 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref>

For his work on [[Laser-wakefield acceleration|laser wakefield acceleration]], Tajima received the [[Nishina Memorial Prize]] in 2006;<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nishina Memorial Prize {{!}} Nishina Memorial Foundation|url=https://www.nishina-mf.or.jp/project_en/kinen_en/|access-date=2020-06-06|language=ja}}</ref> the [[Enrico Fermi Prize]] of the [[Italian Physical Society]] in 2015;<ref>{{Cite web|title=École Polytechnique - Accueil site de l'Ecole Polytechnique|url=https://www.polytechnique.edu/en/content/toshiki-tajima-winner-enrico-fermi-prize|access-date=2020-06-06|website=www.polytechnique.edu|language=en}}</ref> the [[Robert R. Wilson Prize]] of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=2019 Robert R. Wilson Prize for Achievement in the Physics of Particle Accelerators Recipient|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Tajima&first_nm=Toshiki&year=2019|access-date=2020-06-06|website=American Physical Society|language=en}}</ref> the [[Hannes Alfvén Prize]] of the [[European Physical Society]] in 2019;<ref>{{Cite web|title=Award of EPS Alfven Prize 2019 to Victor Malka and Toshiki Tajima - European Physical Society (EPS)|url=https://www.eps.org/blogpost/751263/315809/Award-of-EPS-Alfven-Prize-2019-to-Victor-Malka-and-Toshiki-Tajima|access-date=2020-06-06|website=www.eps.org}}</ref> and the [[Charles Hard Townes Award]] from [[The Optical Society]] in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-02-10|title=The Optical Society Names Toshiki Tajima the 2020 Charles Hard Townes Award Winner|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/about_osa/newsroom/news_releases/2020/the_optical_society_names_toshiki_tajima_the_2020/|access-date=2020-06-06|website=The Optical Society}}</ref>
